![](images/posit-assistant.png){.tool-logo height=84 fig-alt="Posit Assistant logo"}

**Posit Assistant** is an AI agent built into [Positron](positron.qmd). You
chat with it in a panel beside your code, and, unlike a plain chat window, it
can act: it reads the files in your folder, looks at the objects in your R
session, runs R code and shell commands, and edits files. You decide how much
of that it may do without asking.

Posit Assistant needs a language model to work with. In Stat 133 we use the
models that come with [GitHub Copilot](code-completion.qmd).

## 1. Before you start

- Follow the [GitHub Copilot](code-completion.qmd) guide through step 3, so that
  Copilot is on for your GitHub account and connected to Positron. That
  connection is all Posit Assistant needs; there's no separate key.
- Open a project folder in Positron (**File → Open Folder**). Posit Assistant
  works inside the open folder.
- If Positron shows a **Restricted Mode** bar at the top of the window, click
  **Manage**, then **Trust**, so the assistant can run code in this folder.
  Only trust folders you created or cloned yourself.

## 2. Open the chat

Click the **Posit Assistant** icon in the activity bar (the column of icons on
the far left of the window). You can also open the Command Palette
(<kbd>⌘</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> on macOS,
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> on Windows) and run
**View: Show Posit Assistant**.

The chat panel opens with a text box at the bottom.

## 3. Choose a model

Click the **model picker** in the bottom right of the chat box and choose one of the models listed
under **GitHub Copilot**.

Each chat message can use several model requests, because the agent works in
steps. With Copilot Free you get about 50 chat requests a month, so pick a
smaller, cheaper model while you learn. With Copilot Pro (through GitHub
Education) you have more room. GitHub lists which models each plan includes
and how many requests each one costs at
<https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing/copilot-requests>.

If no GitHub Copilot models appear, run **Posit Assistant: Configure AI
Providers** from the Command Palette and check that the GitHub Copilot row is
connected.

## 4. Choose a mode

The **mode picker** in the status bar, at the bottom of the window, sets how
much the assistant may do on its own:

| Mode | What it does | Type |
|------|--------------|------|
| **Ask** | Reads and searches only. It can't edit files or run code; it shows you code to run yourself. | `/ask` |
| **Normal** | Asks for your approval before it runs code or edits a file. | `/normal` |
| **Auto** | A second model approves or rejects each action, and asks you only some of the time. This is the default. | `/auto` |
| **Plan** | Writes a plan for a larger change for you to approve before it starts. | `/plan` |

In this class, use **Ask** or **Normal** while you learn, so that you see every
action before it happens. You can type the command in the chat box or use the
picker, and you can switch at any point in a conversation.

## 5. Have a first conversation

Type a message and press <kbd>Return</kbd>. For example, with a script from a
problem set open:

```
What does each pipeline in this file do?
```

Along with your message, the assistant sends the model **context**:

- **Your R session.** It sees the names and types of the objects in your
  environment, not their values. Click the **eye** icon in the status bar to
  turn this off.
- **Files you mention.** Type `@` in the chat box to pick a file or folder
  from your project. Click the paperclip to attach a file from elsewhere, or
  paste an image.
- **What it looks up.** As it works, it may read more files or run code to
  inspect your data. Each step shows in the chat.

When it wants to run code or change a file (in Normal mode), it shows you
exactly what, with buttons to approve or reject. Read it first. You can also
run something yourself without involving the model: start a message with
`!r` for R code (`!r summary(penguins)`) or `!` for a shell command
(`! git status`), and the result joins the conversation.

## 6. Manage the conversation

- **New chat.** Run **Posit Assistant: New Chat** to start fresh. A new chat
  starts with empty context, which often works better than a long one that has
  wandered.
- **Token counter.** The counter in the status bar shows how much of the
  model's context window the conversation is using. Click it for a breakdown.
  When the conversation gets close to the limit, the assistant summarizes the
  earlier messages to make room.

## Tips

- **Commit before you let it edit.** With your work committed in
  [Git](git.qmd), you can see exactly what the assistant changed
  (`git diff`) and undo it.
- **Check its work with code you understand.** The assistant's answers are
  predictions, like every other model output. Run the code, look at the
  result, and ask yourself whether it's right.
- **Give context, not just a question.** Name the data, the columns, and what
  you've already tried.
- Posit Assistant changes quickly. If a button or command here has a different
  name in your version, see the
  [Posit Assistant docs](https://assistant.posit.co/docs/).
